headline: Bien leads Kenya’s Apple Music chart with “I’ll Be Okay”
body: Kenyan singer and songwriter Bien-Aimé Baraza led the 27 November Apple Music songs chart in Kenya with “I’ll Be Okay.” The song is the ninth track on Alusa Continua, his 17-track second solo album, released a week earlier.
sourceHeadline: Top 100 Songs in Kenya on 27 November 2026 — Apple Music Chart
paragraphs: The credits show how many collaborators went into one of the record’s quieter moments. Bien shares the writing credit with a team that includes Remy Baggins and Cleopatra Mukula, while Bensoul contributes backing vocals.

Elsewhere on the album, Joshua Baraka and The Compozers join Bien on “Don’t Go.” The closer, “Ah,” credits Kenyan pianist Aaron Rimbui among its writers. This ranking is the dated Apple Music snapshot collected by ChartStats.

headline: Dhow races and taarab return to Lamu’s cultural festival
body: Lamu’s 24th Cultural Festival opened on Thursday, 26 November, with three days of events in the Old Town. The programme brings dhow racing, Swahili poetry and coastal music to the island through Saturday.
sourceHeadline: Police ban machetes, knives as Lamu Cultural Festival kicks off
paragraphs: The programme moves between the water and the town. Dhow crews and swimmers compete off the seafront, while the land programme includes donkey races, bao board games and performances of taarab and Goma la Lamu.

The Old Town provides part of the setting for what visitors see and hear. UNESCO lists Lamu for the continuity of its Swahili culture and the coral-stone and mangrove-timber buildings that line its streets. The photograph shows a dhow race from the 2012 festival.

headline: Leevans Linyerera’s painting show enters its final weekend
body: Leevans Linyerera’s A Nation in Session is on view at Nairobi National Museum through Monday, 30 November. The solo exhibition brings together paintings about how political authority is presented and how citizens respond to it.
paragraphs: Linyerera’s work asks viewers to look at the rituals around leadership. In Nairobi’s guide describes a series concerned with power and reverence, where repeated public gestures can say as much as the individual people who make them.
It is a painting show with a specific Kenyan setting. The exhibition is in the museum’s Creativity Gallery. Nairobi Now lists the run as 8–30 November.

references.label: Nairobi Now · exhibition dates and location

headline: Eldoret adds the Sisibo Marathon to Kenya’s road-racing calendar
body: The inaugural Sisibo Marathon is scheduled for 19 December in Eldoret. Organisers announced at the November launch in Kapseret that the winners of the men’s and women’s marathons will each receive KSh 5 million.
sourceHeadline: Sisibo marathon launched in Eldoret with KSh5m prize for winners
paragraphs: Eliud Kipchoge spoke at the launch, which Faith Kipyegon also attended. Kipchoge urged organisers to make the event welcoming to ordinary runners and to pay the athletes promptly. Athletics Kenya president Jackson Tuwei said the race was a chance to build on the country’s existing road races.

The Standard reported that Kipchoge also argued for Kenya to work toward hosting a World Marathon Major. His remarks came as a new race was being added to a city that already has the Eldoret City Marathon.

headline: “Crescent on the Road” puts a matatu crew at the centre of a Kenyan drama
body: A Nairobi accountant takes over her late brother’s matatu in Crescent on the Road, a Kenyan feature directed by Victor Gatonye and Mohamed Zainudin. The film is set to premiere at Unseen Cinema in Kilimani on 5 December.
sourceHeadline: Crescent on the Road Film Premieres in Kilimani
paragraphs: Amina Hilal inherits a vehicle called The Crescent and a family home facing foreclosure. In choosing to keep the matatu on the road, she has to contend with its debts as well as with people who question her place in the industry.

Shirleen Wangari and Zainudin produced the feature. Gatonye previously directed the Kenyan thriller 40 Sticks. The film is set in Eastlands, making a familiar part of Nairobi’s daily commute the setting for questions about family, faith and work.

headline: Kenyan Fashion Story puts the business behind the runway on show
body: Kenyan designers will show their work at Karen Village on Saturday, 28 November, at The Kenyan Fashion Story. This year’s programme pairs the runway with discussions about finding customers and building fashion businesses in Kenya.
sourceHeadline: Kenyan Fashion Story 2026 targets new markets for local fashion talent
paragraphs: Founder Ingred Awuor told Citizen Digital the event brings together the people involved in putting a collection in front of an audience, including designers, models, stylists and photographers. Organisers say the discussions will cover the work of pricing, branding and reaching new markets.
The programme also includes fashion and lifestyle exhibitions alongside the collections. The photograph here is from the separate 2015 Faces of Kenya runway show.

headline: Why Lupita Nyong’o plays two sisters in “The Odyssey”
body: Lupita Nyong’o plays Helen of Troy and Clytemnestra in Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey. The director revealed the double casting in May, ahead of the film’s July release.
sourceHeadline: Lupita Nyong’o Will Play 2 Iconic Characters in Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey, Director Confirms
paragraphs: Helen and Clytemnestra are sisters in Greek mythology, married to the brothers Menelaus and Agamemnon. Their marriages tie them to different parts of the Trojan War and its aftermath. Casting Nyong’o in both parts gives those stories a shared face.

Nolan adapted Homer’s epic about Odysseus’s journey home after the war. Matt Damon leads the cast as Odysseus, with Nyong’o appearing alongside performers including Tom Holland and Anne Hathaway. Universal says the film will return to cinemas in the United States and Canada on 11 December.

headline: Kodong Klan brings All Hands On Deck to Nairobi
body: Kodong Klan will play Nairobi’s ASK Grounds on 28 November. The concert features solo sets from members of the Kenyan collective, a joint finale and a guest performance by Keteh.
sourceHeadline: Sunquick backs Kodong Klan's 'All Hands-on Deck' Nairobi concert
paragraphs: Bensoul, Charisma, Coster Ojwang, Mordecai Dex, Okello Max, Onyach Pala and Ywaya Tajiri are on the bill, according to Music In Africa. Keteh will bring songs from Safari Ya Mapenzi, including Umebant.

headline: Ibraah’s “Usela” tops Apple Music’s Tanzania chart
sourceHeadline: Ibraah’s “Usela” tops Apple Music’s Tanzania chart
body: Ibraah is at No. 1 in Apple Music’s 27 November Tanzania update. His track “Usela” leads the storefront’s most-played songs list.
paragraphs: “Tse Monate” is second. The track credits Diamond Platnumz, Xduppy and DJ Maphorisa, alongside Focalistic, Uncool MC, Angekebabuye mc and Ricky Lenyora.
The list measures activity on Apple Music in Tanzania. Apple’s feed provides ranking positions and track credits.

headline: Where to find recordings of Somali music, poetry and radio
sourceHeadline: Where to find recordings of Somali music, poetry and radio
body: Somalia’s recorded culture has a home online through the Somali Studies Centre at Roma Tre University. Its archive includes traditional music, spoken poetry, radio broadcasts from Mogadishu and recordings of plays.
paragraphs: Music In Africa’s directory traces the collection to research collaborations with Somali institutions. It describes traditional recordings collected by Francesco Giannattasio and conversations recorded in the 1980s with members of the Academy of Arts and Science in Mogadishu.
For listeners exploring Somali music beyond current releases, the collection gives a starting point for hearing how music, radio and spoken word were recorded alongside one another.

headline: Nairobi City Thunder’s BAL campaign ends against Patriots
body: Nairobi City Thunder lost 83–75 to South Sudan’s Patriots in their final group game at Kasarani Indoor Arena. The defeat ended the Kenyan champions’ bid to qualify for the 2027 Basketball Africa League.
paragraphs: Patriots advanced to the semifinals. FIBA reported that the club won three games in this stage of qualifying. Coach Ajou Deng described the milestone after the game.
> This is the first time we [South Sudan clubs] have won three games in the Road to BAL.
— Ajou Deng, Patriots head coach, [speaking to FIBA](https://www.fiba.basketball/en/news/hosts-thunder-knocked-out-of-the-2027-bal-race)

Thunder had reached the league after hosting the East Division qualifiers in each of the previous two years. The club’s squad includes **Taylor Ongwae**, pictured here during his earlier college career.
sourceHeadline: Heartbreak as Thunder crash out of 2027 BAL race on home soil

headline: Racheal Magoola is bringing “Still Shining” to Kingdom Kampala
body: Kingdom Kampala will host Racheal Magoola for a concert called “Still Shining”, according to Matooke Republic. The concert marks 60th birthday and 40 years in music, the outlet reports.
sourceHeadline: Kingdom Kampala to host Racheal Magoola’s ‘Still Shining’ Concert as singer celebrates 60th birthday and 40 years in music
paragraphs: The show is called **Still Shining**. Matooke Republic says it marks two milestones for the singer, her 60th birthday and four decades in music.
The venue named in the report is **Kingdom Kampala**.

headline: Nikita Kering visits Tyler Perry Studios in Atlanta
sourceHeadline: Nikita Kering visits Tyler Perry Studios in Atlanta
body: Kenyan singer-songwriter Nikita Kering visited Tyler Perry Studios during a trip to the United States. TNX Africa and Mpasho both reported the Atlanta stop.
paragraphs: TNX Africa linked the visit to the **International Visitor Leadership Program**, a U.S. State Department exchange programme. It described the trip in the context of opportunities for Kenya’s creative economy.
The studio visit brought the Kenyan musician into a film and television setting. The photo on this page is from an earlier Capital FM interview.

headline: Diamond Platnumz and his collaborators take “Tse Monate” to No. 2 in Tanzania
sourceHeadline: Diamond Platnumz and his collaborators take “Tse Monate” to No. 2 in Tanzania
body: “Tse Monate” by Diamond Platnumz, Xduppy and DJ Maphorisa reached No. 2 in Apple Music’s Tanzania chart update for 27 November.
paragraphs: The collaboration was released on **30 October 2026**. Apple Music credits Focalistic, Uncool MC, Angekebabuye mc and Ricky Lenyora as featured performers.
The ranking refers to plays on Apple Music in Tanzania. Soundcharts also listed the song at No. 2 in its 27 November chart.

headline: Aar Maanta brings dhaanto and qaraami into his own sound
sourceHeadline: Aar Maanta brings dhaanto and qaraami into his own sound
body: Somali-British musician Aar Maanta brings different strands of Somali music into the same set. His catalogue draws on **dhaanto** and **qaraami**, according to his Music In Africa profile.
paragraphs: Greenbelt’s artist profile traces his collaborations across generations and genres. It names Somali singers **Maryam Mursal** and **Ahmed “Hudeydi” Ismail Hussein** alongside Algerian raï singer Abdelkader Saadoun.
Aar Maanta is a useful starting point for listeners exploring how Somali music travels between East Africa and the diaspora. The photo shows the artist.
